headline: Approved $300,000 school energy upgrades and $34,291.49 virus protection contract; rejected emergency vote on federal police corruption probe.
summary: Public speakers and councilors spent much of the meeting debating a resolution asking the U.S. Attorney to reopen the case against former police leadership. The councilors voted 4-5 against the emergency preamble on that resolution. The council also approved annual reviews for its clerks and solicitor by an 8-1 vote, and it questioned trash collection costs at Housing Authority properties.
decisions: Removed contracts C-27-34 and C-27-37 from the agenda, as the Mayor recommended.
Approved vehicle-for-hire company license for Zanr Transportation, LLC, unanimously.
Approved a $34,291.49 virus protection contract with EPlus Technology, Inc., unanimously.
Approved a $300,000 energy and building upgrade contract for Timony Grammer School, unanimously.
Approved ordering a state election for November 3, 2026, unanimously.
Approved annual performance evaluations for council employees, 8-1, with Clr. Simard voting no.
Failed 4-5 to approve the emergency preamble on the resolution asking federal authorities to reopen the Methuen police corruption investigation.
Approved, unanimously, the emergency preamble for the resolution accepting a $7,500 Catalyst Fund grant for the Little Free Pantry Initiative.
Approved accepting a gift of 9/11 memorial banners, unanimously.
Approved, unanimously, adding a new Sealer of Weights and Measurers position to the wage and salary plan.

Court used the 8th Amendment for unfair treatment. So, they gave this Lieutenant his

Fenton Court versus PERAC, to justify getting their pensions back. So, you're going to 
end up having to pay him back eventually. It's just a matter of time. This case was 
mishandled by the prosecution. It was underplayed. It was under charge. There's not a 
single count that was charged for false arrest, unlawful search and seizure, unlawful 
confinement, impersonating a police officer. These are all things that Sean (Fountain) 
was. And when Sean (Fountain) pled guilty last December, he admitted to all of that by 
pleading guilty to those. So, every arrest that Sean Fountain made, you are now 
currently on the hook for from a civil liability standpoint. Every summons, every 
speeding ticket, the liability here is massive. And now you have a connection to the 
MPTC. I suggest that you were laid out by the state to be the sole victim here. That's 
why they didn't charge up inappropriately, or in my professional opinion. Now there's a 
52-page document that comes from the Records Director from MPTC, goes to show that 
they were complicit in helping or accusing the MPTC of helping create the forged

launch of our new Little Free Pantry Initiative. I want to give kudos to Director of Public 
Health Caeli Tegan Zampach and her team for working hard to advance this effort to help 
tackle the issue of food insecurity in our community. Little Free Pantry concept is a turn on the 
popular Little Free Library movement, a community book sharing box intended to remove 
barriers to book access and be available to all 24-7. The Little Free Pantry is the same idea but 
for non-perishable food. It is a donation-based self-sustaining initiative where neighbors can take 
items they need and leave what they can. The pantries would contain shelf-stable food, 
community resources, and health education materials. The outpouring of generosity and 
community support from the Methuen Cares Emergency Food Drive in November 2025, 
including donations and volunteers, indicates that our community would be interested in and 
willing to participate in the Little Free Pantry Initiative. We expect this project to foster a sense 
of community in Methuen, motivating neighbors to help neighbors in public or private 
properties can install and host a Little Free Pantry. We plan to place these pantries in public 
locations and areas that are easy to access, are in lower income, areas that are densely 
populated, and have demonstrated food insecurity.

and address the recurring deficits associated with the City's Health Insurance Trust Fund. The 
special enrollment period started today and will run through October 30, 2026. Anyone wishing 
to have GIC coverage effective January 1 must apply during that period. Enrollment is not

I'm very excited about the Methuen Literacy Partnerships' new BookBuddy program, which is 
launching at the Tenney School this school year. It's a pen pal style program that matches third 
graders with volunteers in the community who provide three new books and three handwritten 
literacy themed letters over the course of the year with students writing back after each 
exchange. The books are theirs to keep and all exchanges are coordinated through the 
partnership. This is a wonderful opportunity to help a child develop a love of reading while 
letting them know that someone in their community is rooting for them. I'm a strong supporter 
of this effort and I encourage counselors and residents to consider joining me and becoming a 
BookBuddy. You can learn more and sign up at methuenreads.org.  
Last Friday marked the opening of the YWCA Northeastern Massachusetts' new Domestic 
Violence and Sexual Assault Services Office at 5 Wallace Street. This is a full circle moment 
for our community. As you may recall, 5 Wallace Street was ground zero in our fight against 
human trafficking in Methuen last year and now today a location associated with the human 
trafficking operation has become a place where survivors can receive counseling, advocacy, and 
support as they rebuild their lives. When we formed the Methuen Human Trafficking Task 
Force, we committed to combating exploitation and supporting survivors. That work continues 
but this new partnership with the YWCA represents an important step forward. I want to thank 
the YWCA and everyone who helped make the transformation possible.  
I'm pleased to report that Methuen's Community Choice Power Supply Program saved 
participating customers more than $1.14 million during the first six months of 2026 compared 
with what they would have paid for electricity supply through National Grids Basic Service. 
Approximately 12,500 consumers participated each month during that period. As I state 
constantly, it seems electricity bills are still too high, and I hear that from residents every single

and that work is producing real tangible savings. Our rate remains fixed at 12.83 cents per 
kilowatt hour through December 2027, roughly 25 percent below National Grids current 
residential basic service supply rate. Future savings depend on how National Grids rates change 
but the savings already achieved are dollars kept in the pockets of people participating in 
Methuen's program. Folks can learn more about the program at colonialpowergroup.com slash
